conviction_note: The release is real but it lands at 13:00 GMT on 4 Nov, inside the London session, not after the close. The quarter holds two milestones already disclosed that the valuation policy requires Burford to mark up: the ICC Cameroon award (24 Jul, more than A$250m, all on the balance sheet) and the Taction v Apple verdict (25 Sep, about $700m on the balance sheet). Against stale consensus EPS of $0.09 and Q2's $0.01, the reported number should beat by a wide margin. But the gain is non-cash, every input is public, the stock rose 13.6% in the 5 sessions before the seal, and Burford's results days have been sold (5 of the last 7 two-day LSE windows negative). So p_up sits only slightly above 50 (54) on a 7% scale, and the scaled +0.56 is smaller than the +1.3 sum of the findings because the reaction history vetoes the direction, not the size.

findings.finding: 3Q26 holds two positive milestones the valuation policy requires Burford to mark up: the ICC Cameroon award (24 Jul, entitlement more than A$250m, 100% balance sheet) and the Taction v Apple jury verdict (25 Sep, about $700m balance-sheet entitlement). The 2Q26 10-Q's policy table gives positive milestone factors of 5-40% for a 'significant ruling ... prior to trial court judgment' and 25-60% for a 'trial court judgment or tribunal award', each closing that share of the gap between cost and forecast proceeds. Even the low end implies an unrealized gain of tens to low hundreds of $m, against a consensus EPS of $0.09 (about $20m) and Burford-only equity of $819m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Big reported-number swings at Burford have mostly been sold or ignored. 2025 results moved -10.45% on the LSE release day; 1Q26 moved -4.47% on D and -7.55% over two days; 2Q26 (EPS $0.01 against $0.08-0.16) moved -0.44% on LSE and +0.70% on NYSE. The Taction verdict itself added only about 9-14 cents on the dollar of the balance-sheet entitlement to the market cap (Legal Special Situations, 2026-10-01).
findings.why_not_priced: The milestones are public; the SIZE of the mark is not, and no source quantifies it. The aggregator consensus of $0.09 shows no markup, and the market valued Taction at about 9-14c on the dollar of the $700m. A mark at the policy's factors would lift book per share by perhaps 10-30% on a stock trading at about 1.0x book ($3.79 against $3.74). If the market had priced a large mark, the stock would not have printed a 12-month low of $3.00 on 16 Oct, three weeks after the verdict. Against that, it rose about 26% off that low into the seal, which may be partly anticipation. The finding is capped because the gain is non-cash, the bar is snippet_only and stale, Apple's post-quarter JMOL gives skeptics a ready reason to discount the mark, and Burford's own release warns 'very few large patent verdicts survive the post-verdict process intact'.
findings.independence: Legal Special Situations (2026-10-01 and 2026-10-05, 'How a $5.7 billion jury award might show up in Burford's next results') makes the same point from outside the company that Burford marks cases up at milestones such as a trial win and that the verdict falls inside Q3: https://legalspecialsituations.substack.com/p/apple-just-lost-a-record-57-billion. Same underlying facts, so not independent evidence about the size.

findings.finding: Financing in the quarter: $300m 8% senior secured 2029 notes, 10x oversubscribed, plus $100m of cash retired the $400m 6.25% 2028 notes. Total debt fell $100m to about $2.3bn, and management flagged further de-leveraging via open-market debt purchases. 3Q interest runs on about $48m a quarter (2Q26 debt interest expense).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The notes launch on 14-16 Sep coincided with LSE falling from 318.8 to 302.8. The 'update on successful capital raise' (18 Sep) moved -2.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: fully disclosed in September. The money bought a maturity extension and a $100m debt cut, not a ramp, so it is neutral. Filed because it bears on 3Q cash and interest; any buybacks of debt in Q3 would be the only new element.

findings.finding: Positioning: US short interest was about 6.9% of float with about 8.5 days to cover (21 Aug 2026; Equibles snippet). The UK register shows nothing at or above 0.5%. Moderate short fuel if the mark surprises upward; the stock rose 13.6% in the 5 days into the seal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 28 Sep the verdict RNS moved +9.4% on LSE and +8.0% on NYSE, with NYSE volume 3.9m, the highest of the month.
findings.why_not_priced: 8.5 days to cover makes a fast squeeze on a large mark plausible. But the figure is 10 weeks stale and snippet_only, and the 5-day run-up may already be covering, so the size is small.

baseline_tension: The finding leans positive against a slightly negative priced lean (-0.30, all run-up). The 5-day run-up of +13.6% agrees with the finding's direction, so part of it may be anticipated. The name's habit of selling results days cuts against it, which is why p_up is only 54.
language_note: The domestic UK RNS channel (Investegate) carried the issuer's exact release timestamp (13:00 GMT, in the London session) that settles the session against the vendor's amc flag; the same text is on Burford's US 8-K/PR Newswire channel, so this is source locality, not information the English wires lacked.

lessons_applied: 'A beat made of a one-off is sold' (H&M) and the carried-over 'verified fact is not a predicted reaction': the fair-value mark is a non-cash gain on public milestones, so the reported-quarter finding went from +2.0 to +1.0 and p_up from 56 to 54.

'Right about the number and too small about the move' (18 of 23): new numbers with no pre-release, so abs_move_pct went up from 6.5 to 7.0 rather than being capped at the name's 2.22% baseline median, which was also measured on the wrong (D+1) window.
'Your own session check ... open with the verdict': session_check now opens with 'bmo' and the issuer timestamp, so the resolver windows close(11-03) -> close(11-04).
